review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the NavierStokes directory for uses of the candidate lemmas. The file has no @[simp] lemmas, and the module has many simp-set lemmas elsewhere. Every algebraic rewrite lemma on torusAverage and graphDr is applied by hand with rw or simp_rw. I found no unwanted expansion and no loops, because nothing is tagged simp. I did not run Lean, so I did not test whether the proposed tags would work, and I may be wrong about downstream interactions. The two findings are modest and depend on how the library prefers to use simp.

findings.excerpt: torusAverage (weightedSource f) p = p.1 * torusAverage f p
findings.problem: These two lemmas push torusAverage through the file's own pointwise operations divideRadius and weightedSource. They have the right orientation for a normal form: the right-hand side is structurally smaller and has no side conditions. Neither lemma is a simp lemma, so every user applies them manually. `torusAverage_weightedSource` is used by `rw` in TemporalMeanUpdate (twice) and GaugeAliasDecay, and by `simp_rw` in this file. `torusAverage_divideRadius` is applied by `rw`. The sibling lemma `torusAverage_pressureSource` is also unattributed. The torusAverage of a `weightedSource` or `divideRadius` therefore has no canonical simp form, and one-off chains like `rw [..., torusAverage_weightedSource, ..., mul_zero]` are needed.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `torusAverage_weightedSource` and `torusAverage_divideRadius` with `@[simp]`. Both are unconditional, and the right-hand side has no `torusAverage (weightedSource _)` or `torusAverage (divideRadius _)` pattern, so they should not loop. `torusAverage_weightedSource` could instead go in a local simp set if a global attribute is considered too broad. Check that `div_eq_mul_inv`-style simp normal forms do not make the `/ p.1` form fight other lemmas.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then discharge goals such as `torusAverage (weightedSource γ) (R, s) = 0` once the zero-mean fact is available. This replaces the `rw [temporalSource, PressureStream.torusAverage_weightedSource, ..., mul_zero]` pattern and the `simp_rw [torusAverage_weightedSource]` at the end of this file.

findings.excerpt: graphDr (physicalSpeed d M) v f p = RadialPullback.physicalGraphDeriv d M v f p := rfl
findings.problem: This bridge lemma between the local `graphDr` with `physicalSpeed` and `RadialPullback.physicalGraphDeriv` is proved by `rfl` and has no simp attribute. It is applied by hand as the first step of three proofs in this file: `meanPressure_radial_residual`, `streamGamma_eq_desired_sub_alias` and `meanPressure_radial_residual_global`. It is also used in VariableGaugeMean. Each proof then needs a second `rw` with a `physicalGraphDeriv_physicalCompact*` lemma. Because it is not a simp lemma, any `simp` call on a `graphDr (physicalSpeed d M) ..` goal cannot reach the RadialPullback API. The `rw` form only works when the term is syntactically `graphDr (physicalSpeed d M) v f p`.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `graphDr_eq_physical` with `@[simp]`, or use a local simp set. The direction is toward the RadialPullback form, which is where the other physicalCompact derivative lemmas live. The LHS head is the file's own definition and cannot be re-produced by the RHS, so a loop is unlikely. Alternatively, state the lemma with `physicalSpeed d M` as a pattern so it fires only for the physical speed.
findings.benefit: Callers get one canonical normal form for the physical radial derivative. The repeated `rw [graphDr_eq_physical, ...]` prefix could become a plain `simp only [graphDr_eq_physical]` or a simp call. It would also work under binders, where `rw` fails.
